view: This print turns on cash and on the FY27 guide, not on Q4 EPS. Q4 is the seasonal cash quarter. Last year's Q4 rose 28% on record operating cash flow ($96M) and a $126M FCF year against a $75-95M guide. The company's record splits cleanly: it over-promises EBITDA (FY25 cut from $385-405M to $360-380M, FY26 steered to the low end) and under-promises cash (FY25 FCF beat its guide by about $30M). My own inputs point toward a solid cash quarter. The plastics-resin PPI spiked from 312.7 in March to 365.0 in May 2026 and then eased to about 332 in July-September (FRED PCU325211325211). Management blamed Q3's working-capital use on that inflation, so the falling resin through Q4 should release working capital and help the $58-78M Q4 FCF. It also gives a small price-cost tailwind on top of the 'couple million' European catch-up management flagged. Customer demand is steady: Kimberly-Clark's North America volumes were +2% in Q3 2026, and Suominen called nonwoven demand stable with EBITDA up. Q4 EBITDA landing near $98-103M and FCF inside the range is therefore the base case, and both are largely public. The open question is the FY27 guide. FY26 ending near $380-385M plus about $20M of carryover gives about $400-405M before inflation and European softness. The one forward figure I found ($409M) sits slightly above that, and management's habit of guiding EBITDA high could cut either way: a higher initial guide pleases on the day. With the equity a thin slice of EV, a 2-3% change in perceived EBITDA moves the shares 10% or more, so the size is large and the direction close to a coin. Cash and the lower bar from the tape-driven slide lean slightly up. Thin estimates that probably sit too high on revenue, and a weak tape into a 13:00 window, lean slightly down.
unpriced: Possibly the working-capital release from resin deflation in the July-September quarter. The PPI shows resin down about 9% from its May peak, and the price only holds the reaffirmed FCF range, not a beat. That is a lead, not a demonstrated gap: I cannot see Q4 receivables or inventory, and the FY27 guide matters more and is not visible.

recommendation.reason: The deciding line is the FY27 EBITDA/FCF guide. Its inputs (FY26 exit about $380-385M plus $20M carryover against a roughly $409M forward figure) land close to where the price and the few estimates sit. The cash tailwind from resin deflation is real but modest and partly expected after the reaffirmation. Nothing gives a 65% edge, and the levered equity and falling tape make an ordinary morning move large in either direction.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Q4 FCF clearly above $110M for the year together with an FY27 EBITDA guide at or above $410M at the midpoint would make an up move likely. An FY27 guide midpoint under $395M, or FCF missing the $90M floor, would make a sharp fall likely.

self_critique: The case for up rests on the cash quarter and the company's record of beating FCF guides, but FCF was already reaffirmed and is the number the market watches, so a delivery inside the range may be fully expected. The CFO's 'work to go' on working capital is a hedge, not a promise. Against that, management has over-guided EBITDA two years running, so an FY27 guide built on synergy carryover could be read sceptically even if it meets the $409M figure. The 13:00 window after a bmo release also catches a falling small-cap tape that has hit this high-beta name hard in the last week. Taken together the case against is about as strong as the case for, which is why p_up stays near 50 and no trade is recommended.
approach_notes: P6's split of the run-in into tape and own news helped: the -10% was mostly IWM beta. Checking the real past reactions against the bars exposed the baseline's misdated history, which had made the 7-of-7 'up' record look like a positive base rate. P7's 'estimate the line from its inputs' was hard here because the FY27 guide has no visible inputs beyond the synergy carryover and one unattributed forward figure.
